challenges.hint: Do the outer rays make a straight line (180°), a right angle (90°), or do two lines cross? Equal opposite angles are vertical.

lesson.intent: Find a missing angle from a relationship

data.title: Solving for Unknown Angles
data.description: Practice using angle relationships such as supplementary, complementary, and vertical angles to determine missing measurements in various geometric figures.

challenges.narration: A tile pattern has two lines crossing.
challenges.instruction: x and the labeled angle are vertical angles. Find x.
challenges.hint: Vertical angles (opposite each other where two lines cross) are equal, so x equals the known angle.

challenges.narration: A signpost has two angles that form a right angle.
challenges.instruction: These two angles are complementary (they add to 90°). Find the unknown angle x.
challenges.hint: Complementary angles add to 90°, so x = 90° − the known angle.

challenges.narration: A tile pattern has two angles that sit on a straight line.
challenges.instruction: These two angles are supplementary (they add to 180°). Find the unknown angle x.
challenges.hint: Angles on a straight line add to 180°, so x = 180° − the known angle.

challenges.narration: A garden trellis has three angles meeting at a point.
challenges.instruction: The three angles go all the way around the point (360°). Find the unknown angle x.
challenges.hint: Angles around a point add to 360°, so x = 360° − the two known angles.

lesson.intent: Write and solve an equation for an unknown angle

results.title: Solving for Unknown Angles with Algebraic Expressions

data.title: Solving for Unknown Angles with Algebraic Expressions
data.description: Practice setting up and solving linear equations to find unknown angle values using geometric relationships.

challenges.narration: A signpost has angles labeled by expressions.
challenges.instruction: These two angles are supplementary (add to 180°). Write an equation and solve for x.
challenges.hint: Add the two expressions, set the sum equal to 180, and solve for x.

challenges.narration: A kite frame has two crossing lines with angles labeled by expressions.
challenges.instruction: These two angles are vertical angles, so they are equal. Set the expressions equal and solve for x.
challenges.hint: Vertical angles are equal: set the two expressions equal to each other, then solve for x.

challenges.narration: A garden trellis has angles labeled by expressions.
challenges.instruction: These two angles are complementary (add to 90°). Write an equation and solve for x.
challenges.hint: Add the two expressions, set the sum equal to 90, and solve for x.

challenges.narration: A bracket on a shelf has two crossing lines with angles labeled by expressions.
challenges.instruction: These two angles are vertical angles, so they are equal. Set the expressions equal and solve for x.
challenges.hint: Vertical angles are equal: set the two expressions equal to each other, then solve for x.

lesson.intent: Find angles formed by a transversal

data.title: Finding Angles Formed by Transversals
data.description: Practice finding unknown angle measures using the geometric relationships formed when parallel lines are cut by a transversal.

challenges.narration: A roof truss forms a triangle.
challenges.instruction: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°. Two are given — find the third, x.
challenges.hint: The angles of any triangle add to 180°, so x = 180° − the two known angles.

challenges.narration: A triangular sail forms a triangle.
challenges.instruction: The three angles of a triangle add to 180°. Two are given — find the third, x.
challenges.hint: The angles of any triangle add to 180°, so x = 180° − the two known angles.

challenges.narration: A ladder leaning across two shelves — two parallel lines cut by a transversal.
challenges.instruction: The marked angle and x are corresponding angles. Find x.
challenges.hint: corresponding angle pairs are equal when the lines are parallel, so x equals the marked angle.

challenges.narration: A ladder leaning across two shelves — two parallel lines cut by a transversal.
challenges.instruction: The marked angle and x are alternate interior angles. Find x.
challenges.hint: alternate interior angle pairs are equal when the lines are parallel, so x equals the marked angle.

challenges.narration: A yield sign has one side extended past a corner.
challenges.instruction: The exterior angle x equals the sum of the two remote interior angles. Find x.
challenges.hint: An exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two non-adjacent (remote) interior angles.
